children: Brazil's gross debt as a share of gross domestic product rose to 82.5% in July from 81.9% a month earlier, central bank data showed on Monday.

The hefty interest bill once again drove the increase — a growing concern for investors and economists who view debt-servicing costs as one of the main fiscal vulnerabilities for Latin America's largest economy.
Despite posting a small primary surplus, the public sector remained deep in the red once interest payments were taken into account.
The primary surplus came to 1.4 billion reais ($270.06 million) in July, well below the 5.6 billion reais median forecast in a Reuters poll of economists.
But interest payments came to 99 billion reais, leading to a nominal deficit of 97.6 billion reais, above the 84 billion reais expected by analysts.
Investors remain skeptical about the government's ability to stabilize public debt as mandatory spending pressures persist and high interest rates continue to push borrowing costs higher.
Over a rolling 12-month period, the primary deficit improved to 0.67% of GDP, largely due to a calendar effect linked to court-ordered payments.
The federal government faces a substantial bill from final court rulings against it. While last year most of those court-ordered payments were made in July, this year they were concentrated in March.
With July 2025's large disbursements dropping out of the 12-month calculation, the fiscal reading improved.
The effect also helped narrow the nominal deficit to 9.34% of GDP for the 12 months through July from 9.99% a month earlier, although the level remains high by historical standards.
